notesStmt.note: This poem was written to commemorate the death of Sheridan, who died August 5, 1888. This draft was therefore written sometime between then and August 12, when the poem was published.

An early draft of a poem that first appeared, without a title, in the New York Herald on August 12, 1888, four days after Whitman's short prose tribute to General Philip K. Sheridan, a Union general during the Civil War. The poem was later published in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891), under the title "Interpolation Sounds."
